questions: Platform components
F1
Cloud Pak foundational services
In CP4I 16.1.0, which component provides identity and access management for the Platform UI, including integration with enterprise identity providers such as LDAP or SAML/OIDC?
Keycloak, provided through IBM Cloud Pak foundational services
Apache ZooKeeper
Red Hat AMQ Broker
Grafana

From recent CP4I releases, including 16.1.0, the Platform UI uses Keycloak (delivered with Cloud Pak foundational services) for authentication. Keycloak can federate LDAP and broker SAML or OIDC identity providers, and CP4I roles are assigned to users and groups there.
Correct: Keycloak provides identity for the Platform UI.
Wrong: ZooKeeper coordinates distributed systems; it is not an identity provider.
Wrong: AMQ Broker is a messaging product.
Wrong: Grafana is a dashboarding tool.
Corporate Active Directory groups are federated into Keycloak and mapped to CP4I integration-admin and integration-developer roles.
Identity questions for 16.1.0: Platform UI -> Keycloak -> enterprise IdP.
Platform components
F1
cert-manager
What is the role of cert-manager in a CP4I 16.1.0 installation?
It manages the cluster's DNS records
It issues and renews TLS certificates for CP4I components based on Issuer and Certificate resources
It stores MQ messages
It scales Kafka partitions

cert-manager automates certificate creation and rotation. CP4I operators create Certificate resources, and cert-manager issues them from Issuers (for example a self-signed CA or an enterprise CA), storing the results in Kubernetes Secrets.
Wrong: DNS is outside cert-manager's role here.
Correct: it issues and renews certificates.
Wrong: MQ stores messages.
Wrong: partition scaling is a Kafka operation.
When the internal CA certificate nears expiry, cert-manager renews it automatically and the operators roll the affected pods.
No cert-manager -> no certificates -> instances fail to reconcile.
Platform components
F1
Cloud Pak for Integration
Which of these is a CP4I instance type that can be created from the Platform UI?
Queue manager
Virtual machine
Hypervisor
Bare-metal host

The Platform UI can create instances such as queue managers, integration runtimes, integration dashboards and designers, API management (API Connect), Event Streams, Event Endpoint Management, Event Processing, enterprise gateways (DataPower), high-speed transfer servers and automation assets.
Correct: a queue manager is a CP4I instance type.
Wrong: VMs are not CP4I instances.
Wrong: hypervisors are infrastructure.
Wrong: hosts are infrastructure.
A developer creates a 'quick start' non-production queue manager from the Platform UI to try a new application.
Know the list of instance types. It appears often in overview questions.
Platform components
F1
App Connect Enterprise
What is the App Connect Dashboard used for in CP4I?
Uploading BAR files and managing integration runtimes and servers through a web UI
Monitoring Kafka consumer lag
Managing API products
Configuring OpenShift nodes
The App Connect Dashboard is a UI for managing ACE deployments in containers: uploading BAR files, creating integration runtimes, and managing configuration objects.
Correct: it manages BAR files, runtimes and configurations.
Wrong: consumer lag is an Event Streams concern.
Wrong: API products are managed in API Connect.
Wrong: node configuration is OpenShift administration.
Developers upload a BAR to the Dashboard's content server, then deploy a runtime that references it.
Dashboard = deploy and manage. Designer = author flows. Toolkit = desktop development.
Platform components
F1
App Connect Designer
Which tool lets business-oriented integrators build event- and API-driven flows to SaaS applications with a browser-based, low-code experience in CP4I?
App Connect Designer
DataPower WebGUI
MQ Explorer
OpenShift CLI

App Connect Designer (the DesignerAuthoring instance) provides browser-based, low-code authoring of flows that connect SaaS and enterprise applications. Flows can be exported and run in integration runtimes.
Correct: Designer is the low-code flow authoring tool.
Wrong: the DataPower WebGUI administers gateways.
Wrong: MQ Explorer administers MQ objects.
Wrong: oc is a command-line tool, not low-code authoring.
A marketing analyst builds a flow that creates Salesforce leads from new Marketo contacts in Designer, and IT deploys it to an integration runtime.
Low-code SaaS flows -> Designer. Complex enterprise flows -> ACE Toolkit.

Automation assets
What does the Automation assets capability (asset repository) provide in CP4I?
A repository to store, share, discover and reuse integration assets such as APIs, schemas, flows and other artifacts across teams
A runtime for executing BPMN processes
Block storage for Kafka
A CI server
Automation assets lets teams publish and discover reusable integration assets, for example API definitions, message models, flows and mappings, so they are not rebuilt from scratch.
Correct: it is a shared repository for reusable integration assets.
Wrong: it does not run BPMN workflows.
Wrong: it does not provide storage to Kafka.
Wrong: it is not a CI server.
A team publishes a canonical Customer schema and a standard error-handling subflow; other squads find and reuse them.
Automation assets is about reuse and discovery, not runtime execution.

A developer asks where to find connection details and links for all instances they are allowed to see across several namespaces. What should they use?
The CP4I Platform UI
The MQ console only
The OpenShift node terminal
The License Service report
The Platform UI lists the instances the user is authorized to see across namespaces and links to each capability's management UI.
Correct: the Platform UI provides an instance overview.
Wrong: the MQ console shows only queue manager details.
Wrong: node terminals are for platform administrators and debugging.
Wrong: License Service reports usage, not endpoints.
A new team member logs into the Platform UI and sees the dev queue manager, the Event Streams instance and the API Manager link that their role allows.
Platform UI visibility depends on assigned roles and namespace access.
Platform components
T2
cert-manager
After installing CP4I operators, every new instance remains in a 'Pending' or 'not ready' state and events show that Certificate resources cannot be processed. What is the MOST likely cause?
The cert-manager Operator is not installed or not running
The entitlement key is too long
The cluster has too many worker nodes
The browser cache is full
CP4I 16.1.0 instances rely on cert-manager to issue certificates. If cert-manager is missing or unhealthy, Certificate resources are never fulfilled, Secrets are not created, and pods cannot start.
Correct: missing cert-manager blocks certificate issuance.
Wrong: key length does not matter here.
Wrong: node count does not cause this.
Wrong: client caching is unrelated.
oc get certificates -n cp4i shows READY=False; installing the cert-manager Operator for Red Hat OpenShift resolves it.
Certificate resources stuck -> check cert-manager health first.
Platform components
T2
Cloud Pak foundational services
Users report they cannot log into the Platform UI, but the OpenShift console works. Which component should the administrator check FIRST?
The Keycloak (foundational services identity) pods and their connection to the configured identity provider
The MQ channel status
Kafka partition leaders
The DataPower crypto profile
Platform UI authentication goes through Keycloak. If Keycloak is down, misconfigured, or cannot reach the enterprise LDAP or IdP, Platform UI logins fail even though OpenShift OAuth still works.
Correct: Platform UI login depends on Keycloak.
Wrong: channels do not affect UI login.
Wrong: Kafka leaders do not affect UI login.
Wrong: DataPower settings are unrelated.
The LDAP bind password stored in Keycloak's federation configuration had expired; updating it restored logins.
Separate the two identity paths: OpenShift OAuth for the cluster console, Keycloak for the Platform UI.

Cloud Pak for Integration
Which registry hosts IBM entitled CP4I container images?
cp.icr.io (IBM Entitled Registry)
docker.io/library
quay.io/openshift-release-dev only
registry.redhat.io only
Entitled CP4I images are served from cp.icr.io/cp/... and need entitlement-key authentication. Some open images come from icr.io.
Correct: cp.icr.io is the IBM Entitled Registry.
Wrong: Docker Hub does not host entitled CP4I images.
Wrong: that repository hosts OpenShift release images.
Wrong: Red Hat's registry hosts Red Hat images, not entitled IBM images.
A firewall request lists cp.icr.io and icr.io as required egress for connected installations.
Firewall planning for connected installs: allow cp.icr.io and icr.io.
Installation planning
F1
Cloud Pak for Integration
What is the purpose of the 'oc ibm-pak' plugin in CP4I installation?
It downloads CASE packages and generates mirror manifests and catalog sources, for example for air-gapped installations
It is a text editor
It replaces the oc CLI
It configures Kafka ACLs

The ibm-pak plugin works with IBM CASE (Container Application Software for Enterprises) packages. It lists images, generates image-mirroring manifests, and creates CatalogSource and ImageContentSourcePolicy/ImageDigestMirrorSet resources.
Correct: it manages CASE-based mirroring and catalog resources.
Wrong: it is not an editor.
Wrong: it is a plugin that extends oc.
Wrong: Kafka ACLs are configured through Event Streams.
The team runs oc ibm-pak get, then oc ibm-pak generate mirror-manifests, to prepare a disconnected install.
Air-gap tooling: ibm-pak -> mirror images -> apply mirror policy and catalog sources.
Installation planning
S2
Cloud Pak for Integration
A team wants a quick evaluation of several CP4I capabilities in a non-production cluster with minimal effort. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
Use small, non-production deployment profiles or samples (for example single-replica instances with ephemeral or minimal storage) from the Platform UI
Deploy production HA profiles for everything
Build all capabilities from source
Use a production cluster shared with customers
Evaluation and development benefit from small, non-HA profiles that consume fewer resources and less license entitlement. HA profiles belong in production.
Correct: small, non-production profiles suit evaluations.
Wrong: HA profiles waste resources for an evaluation.
Wrong: CP4I capabilities are delivered as images, not built from source.
Wrong: never evaluate in a customer-facing production cluster.
An architect stands up a one-replica Event Streams and a quick-start queue manager in an hour to prototype a design.
Development and evaluation = small profiles. Production = HA profiles.
Installation planning
T3
Operator Lifecycle Manager
An operator subscription shows 'ResolutionFailed' with a constraint error mentioning a dependency on another operator version. What is the MOST likely cause?
The catalog sources do not provide a compatible combination of operator versions (for example a missing or outdated dependency catalog)
The worker nodes need more disk
The Platform UI password is wrong
There are too many routes

OLM resolves dependencies between operators. If the required version of a dependency (for example foundational services or another IBM operator) is not available in an enabled CatalogSource, or conflicts with an installed version, resolution fails.
Correct: missing or conflicting catalog content breaks dependency resolution.
Wrong: disk space does not cause OLM resolution errors.
Wrong: UI credentials are unrelated.
Wrong: route count is unrelated.
Adding the missing pinned catalog source for the dependency, as listed in the 16.1.0 documentation, cleared the ResolutionFailed condition.
OLM errors: read the Subscription and InstallPlan conditions; they name the unmet constraint.
Installation planning
T3
Cloud Pak for Integration
An instance's pods are Pending with the event '0/6 nodes are available: insufficient memory'. The namespace has no ResourceQuota. What should the architect do?
Add worker capacity, reduce instance requests by choosing an appropriate profile, or free resources on existing nodes
Delete cert-manager
Change the route hostname
Recreate the entitlement key

The scheduler cannot find a node with enough allocatable memory for the pod's requests. Fix the mismatch by adding capacity, lowering requests (for example a smaller profile in non-production), or freeing resources.
Correct: capacity or requests must be adjusted.
Wrong: cert-manager does not affect scheduling.
Wrong: routes do not affect scheduling.
Wrong: pull secrets do not cause insufficient-memory events.
Moving the dev API Connect instance from a 3-replica to a 1-replica profile let the pods schedule.
'Insufficient memory/cpu' -> requests versus allocatable capacity, not limits.
Upgrade and migration
F1
Cloud Pak for Integration
Which field in most CP4I instance custom resources specifies the product (operand) version to run?
spec.version
metadata.uid
status.phase
spec.nodeName
Instance CRs use spec.version to declare which product version the operator should deploy. Changing it triggers an upgrade when the operator supports the target.
Correct: spec.version controls the operand version.
Wrong: uid is a system-assigned identifier.
Wrong: status is written by the operator, not the user.
Wrong: not a CP4I instance version field.
A pipeline bumps spec.version on the QueueManager CR from one MQ fix level to the next.
Desired state lives in spec. status shows observed state.
Upgrade and migration
S2
API Connect
An organization runs API Connect v10 on VMware (OVA) and wants to move to API Connect in CP4I 16.1.0. Which approach is generally used?
Copy the OVA disk image into a pod
Back up or extract the configuration and migrate it to the new deployment form factor using IBM's documented migration tooling and process, then cut over gateways and DNS
Start fresh and ask every API consumer to re-register with no data migration
Use Aspera to transfer the running VM

Moving API Connect between form factors (OVA to containers in CP4I) follows IBM's documented migration process, which extracts management and portal data and loads it into the target. Gateway endpoints are then switched over in a controlled way.
Wrong: VM images cannot run as pods.
Correct: use the documented migration path and a controlled cut-over.
Wrong: losing consumer subscriptions causes major disruption.
Wrong: Aspera transfers files; it does not migrate running platforms.
The team rehearses the migration twice in a staging cluster, then switches the DNS for api.company.com during a weekend window.
Form-factor migration = export/import using IBM tooling, not copying VMs.
Upgrade and migration
T3
IBM MQ
After upgrading a queue manager's spec.version, the pod restarts and the queue manager fails to start, logging that the data was created by a newer command level and cannot be used. What happened?
The team attempted to downgrade the queue manager to an older MQ version than the one that last ran it, which MQ does not support once the command level has been raised
The PVC was too large
A channel was stopped
The license was set to NonProduction

After MQ starts at a new command level, its data is migrated and older versions cannot use it. Downgrades are not supported without restoring from a backup taken before the upgrade. Rollback planning must account for this.
Correct: downgrade after a command-level change is not possible.
Wrong: PVC size does not cause version errors.
Wrong: channel state does not stop startup.
Wrong: the license use type does not affect data compatibility.
The team restores the queue manager from the backup taken before the upgrade, then redesigns its rollback plan.
Many integration products migrate data forward on upgrade. 'Rollback' often means 'restore from backup'.
Upgrade and migration
S3
Event Streams
A team upgrades Event Streams. Which practice keeps producers and consumers available during the upgrade?
Ensure topics have replication factor 3 with min.insync.replicas 2, so brokers can be rolled one at a time while partitions stay available
Set replication factor 1 to speed the upgrade
Stop all consumers before upgrading
Delete topics and recreate them afterwards
The operator performs rolling restarts. With RF=3 and min.insync.replicas=2, each partition keeps a leader and enough in-sync replicas while one broker restarts, so acks=all producers keep working.
Correct: replication allows rolling upgrades without downtime.
Wrong: RF=1 means partitions go offline when their broker restarts.
Wrong: stopping consumers causes unnecessary outage.
Wrong: deleting topics loses data.
During the rolling upgrade, client metrics show brief leader elections but no failed produce requests.
Rolling upgrades need redundancy. RF=3 and min ISR=2 is the standard production setting.
Enterprise integration patterns
F1
Cloud Pak for Integration
Which enterprise integration pattern decouples a sender from a receiver in time, so the receiver does not need to be available when the message is sent?
Asynchronous messaging (message channel/queue)
Synchronous request-response over HTTP
Shared database polling every millisecond
Remote procedure call with no timeout
Asynchronous messaging through a queue or channel stores the message until the receiver is ready, decoupling availability and processing speed.
Correct: queues decouple sender and receiver in time.
Wrong: synchronous calls require both parties to be available.
Wrong: tight polling of a shared database is a coupling anti-pattern.
Wrong: RPC is synchronous coupling.
An order system drops orders onto a queue; warehouse systems consume them when they come back online after maintenance.
'Receiver not available' points to queueing (MQ).
Enterprise integration patterns
F1
App Connect Enterprise
What does the 'content-based router' pattern do?
Routes a message to different destinations based on the data in the message
Encrypts messages
Stores files on disk
Generates API documentation
A content-based router inspects message content (for example country or order type) and selects the destination. In ACE it is implemented with Route or Filter nodes, ESQL, or a mapping.
Correct: routing based on message content.
Wrong: encryption is a security function.
Wrong: storage is not routing.
Wrong: documentation generation is unrelated.
Orders with priority=express go to the express-fulfilment queue; others go to standard.
Name the pattern: content-based router, splitter, aggregator, translator.
Enterprise integration patterns
F1
App Connect Enterprise
Which pattern collects related messages (for example responses from several back ends) and combines them into a single message?
Aggregator
Splitter
Wire tap
Dead-letter channel
An aggregator correlates related messages and combines them. ACE provides aggregation nodes (AggregateControl/Request/Reply) and other techniques for this.
Correct: the aggregator combines related messages.
Wrong: a splitter does the opposite and breaks one message into many.
Wrong: a wire tap copies messages for monitoring.
Wrong: a dead-letter channel holds undeliverable messages.
A quote request fans out to three insurers, and the replies are aggregated into one comparison response.
Splitter = 1 to N. Aggregator = N to 1.
Enterprise integration patterns
S2
IBM MQ
Which pattern ensures that messages that cannot be processed after repeated attempts are moved aside rather than blocking a queue?
Dead-letter channel / backout queue
Message filter
Content enricher
Claim check
A dead-letter channel or backout queue isolates poison messages so other messages continue to flow. MQ supports backout queues (BOQNAME/BOTHRESH) and the dead-letter queue.
Correct: poison messages are moved aside.
Wrong: filters drop unwanted messages by rule; they do not handle failed processing.
Wrong: enrichers add data.
Wrong: claim check stores large payloads externally.
After 3 failed attempts, a malformed order moves to ORDERS.BACKOUT, and an operator investigates while normal flow continues.
Poison message questions -> backout threshold plus backout queue.
Enterprise integration patterns
S3
Event Streams
A payload of several megabytes must pass through Kafka, but the brokers are tuned for small messages. Which pattern is MOST appropriate?
Claim check: store the payload in object storage and publish a small event containing a reference to it
Increase max.message.bytes to 1 GB on all topics
Split each payload into 10,000 tiny events without correlation
Send the payload by email
The claim-check pattern keeps the event stream lightweight: the large payload goes to object storage, and the event carries a reference (URI plus metadata) that consumers use to fetch it.
Correct: claim check avoids large messages in Kafka.
Wrong: very large messages hurt broker memory and replication.
Wrong: uncorrelated splitting makes reassembly unreliable.
Wrong: not an integration pattern.
Scanned documents go to S3-compatible storage; a document-received event with the object key is published to Kafka.
Large payloads + streaming -> claim check.
Integration lifecycle
S2
Cloud Pak for Integration
Which practice BEST supports a repeatable integration lifecycle (develop, test, deploy) on CP4I?
CI/CD pipelines (for example OpenShift Pipelines/Tekton) that build artifacts such as BAR files and images, run automated tests, and deploy CRs to each environment through GitOps
Manual deployment through UIs in production
Developers editing production configurations directly
Deploying only on Fridays without testing
Automated pipelines build, test and promote versioned artifacts and declarative CRs. GitOps keeps environment state in Git for auditability and rollback.
Correct: CI/CD plus GitOps gives repeatable lifecycle management.
Wrong: manual production changes are error-prone and unaudited.
Wrong: direct production edits bypass governance.
Wrong: deploying without testing is risky.
A commit triggers a Tekton pipeline that builds the BAR, runs unit tests, builds a custom ACE image, and opens a pull request to bump the image tag in the UAT repository.
Pipeline answers should include build, test and promote with declarative configuration.
Integration lifecycle
S3
App Connect Enterprise
A team must decide how to package ACE flows for CP4I deployment. Which TWO options are valid patterns? (Select TWO.)
Reference BAR files from a URL (for example a content server or an artifact repository) in the IntegrationRuntime CR
Build a custom container image that includes the BAR files (baked image) and reference that image
Paste ESQL directly into the OpenShift web console
Deploy BAR files by copying them into a running pod with oc cp

ACE in CP4I supports referencing BARs by URL, for example from the Dashboard content server or an external repository, and also baking BARs into a custom image for immutable deployments. Copying files into running pods is not durable.
Correct: BAR URLs are a supported deployment pattern.
Correct: a baked custom image is a supported immutable pattern.
Wrong: ESQL is compiled into BARs, not entered in the console.
Wrong: oc cp changes vanish on pod restart and are unmanaged.
A regulated team uses baked images signed in their pipeline; an agile team uses BAR URLs pointing at Artifactory.
Immutable and signed -> baked image. Flexible and faster -> BAR URL.
Integration lifecycle
T2
App Connect Enterprise
A newly deployed integration runtime starts, but its flows are not deployed and the logs show it cannot download the BAR file (HTTP 401). What is the MOST likely issue?
The barURL credentials are missing or incorrect (for example the barauth configuration)
The PVC is RWX
Kafka is unavailable
The Platform UI theme is wrong
When BARs are fetched from an authenticated repository, the runtime needs credentials through a configuration object (for example the barauth type). A 401 means authentication failed.
Correct: BAR download credentials are wrong or missing.
Wrong: storage access mode does not cause HTTP 401.
Wrong: Kafka does not serve BAR files.
Wrong: UI themes are irrelevant.
Creating a barauth configuration with the Artifactory token and referencing it from the runtime fixed the issue.
HTTP 401 on BAR download -> barauth configuration.
Architecture governance
S2
API Connect
How can an enterprise enforce API design standards (naming, security definitions, documentation) consistently before APIs are published?
Use API governance or linting rulesets (for example the API Connect governance capability or pipeline linting) as a gate in the publishing process
Ask developers to remember the standards
Allow unrestricted publishing to production catalogs
Disable API security definitions to simplify
Automated governance checks such as rulesets evaluated in API Connect or in a CI pipeline make standards enforceable and auditable.
Correct: automated validation enforces standards.
Wrong: manual memory does not scale or audit.
Wrong: uncontrolled publishing leads to inconsistent or insecure APIs.
Wrong: removing security is unacceptable.
A pipeline fails when an OpenAPI document lacks a securitySchemes entry or uses non-kebab-case paths.
Governance = automated, enforced at publish time.
Architecture governance
D3
Cloud Pak for Integration
An enterprise wants integration teams to self-provision non-production CP4I instances but restrict production changes. Which control set is MOST appropriate?
Self-service namespaces with edit roles and quotas for non-production; production changes only through approved pipelines with GitOps, with read-only human access
Cluster-admin for all developers in all environments
No access to non-production
Shared admin passwords
Least privilege with self-service in lower environments and pipeline-only change in production balances speed with control. Quotas stop any one team from exhausting shared capacity.
Correct: self-service with guardrails, controlled production.
Wrong: cluster-admin for everyone violates least privilege.
Wrong: blocking non-production stifles delivery.
Wrong: shared passwords destroy accountability.
Developers create queue managers in cp4i-dev-<team> within a 16-CPU quota; production QueueManager CRs change only through pull requests.
Pick answers that combine self-service, quotas, least privilege and audited production change.
Hybrid integration
S2
IBM MQ
An application in a public cloud must reliably send messages to a mainframe queue manager on premises. Which solution is MOST appropriate?
A queue manager in CP4I in the cloud with sender/receiver channels (TLS) to the on-premises queue manager, so messages are stored and forwarded across network interruptions
Direct HTTP calls to the mainframe with no retry
Writing to a shared NFS drive
Emailing the messages
MQ store-and-forward between queue managers over secure channels provides assured delivery across WAN links. If the link drops, messages wait on the transmission queue until the channel restarts.
Correct: MQ channels provide assured store-and-forward delivery.
Wrong: no assured delivery or resilience.
Wrong: file sharing over a WAN is fragile and unsafe.
Wrong: not a valid integration pattern.
Cloud payment requests reach the z/OS queue manager through TLS-secured channels; during a 10-minute network blip messages queue up and then flow.
Hybrid plus reliable delivery -> queue manager-to-queue manager channels.
Hybrid integration
S3
Event Streams
A company wants events generated in an on-premises Kafka cluster to be available to analytics in a cloud Event Streams instance with minimal custom code. Which approach is BEST?
Use geo-replication or MirrorMaker 2 to replicate selected topics from the source cluster to the target
Write a custom script that reads log files on broker disks
Have every producer write to both clusters synchronously
Copy PV snapshots every hour
MirrorMaker 2, the basis of Event Streams geo-replication, replicates topics and consumer offsets between Kafka clusters asynchronously and is managed declaratively.
Correct: MirrorMaker 2 / geo-replication is the standard approach.
Wrong: reading broker files directly is unsupported and fragile.
Wrong: dual writes add latency and consistency problems.
Wrong: snapshots are not a replication strategy for live streams.
Topics matching orders.* replicate from the data center cluster to the cloud for the data science team.
Cluster-to-cluster Kafka replication -> MirrorMaker 2.
Enterprise use cases
S2
IBM MQ
A stock trading system requires that each order instruction is processed exactly once, in a transaction that also updates a database. Which technology characteristic matters MOST?
MQ transactional messaging with syncpoint, coordinated with the database (two-phase commit or careful compensation)
Kafka log compaction
An HTTP 200 response
Aspera FASP

MQ supports units of work: messages got under syncpoint are not removed until commit. With XA coordination or a well-designed idempotent pattern, the message and the database update commit or roll back together.
Correct: transactional get and put under syncpoint, coordinated with the database.
Wrong: compaction retains the latest value per key; it does not provide transactions with a database.
Wrong: an HTTP 200 gives no transactional guarantees.
Wrong: Aspera is unrelated.
The order service gets a message under syncpoint, updates DB2, and commits both; a crash before commit means the message is redelivered.
'Exactly once with a database' -> transactions or syncpoint (and possibly XA).
Enterprise use cases
S3
Cloud Pak for Integration
A retailer wants partners to receive real-time inventory-change notifications instead of polling a REST API every second. Which approach is MOST appropriate in CP4I?
Publish inventory changes to Event Streams and offer them to partners through Event Endpoint Management with the Event Gateway
Increase the API rate limit so partners can poll faster
Let partners connect to the inventory database
Send nightly CSV files via Aspera
Event-driven exposure removes wasteful polling and delivers changes in near real time. EEM provides governed, self-service partner access to topics.
Correct: governed event subscription replaces polling.
Wrong: faster polling wastes resources and still lags.
Wrong: direct database access is insecure and tightly coupled.
Wrong: nightly batches are not real time.
A partner subscribes to inventory-changes in the EEM catalog and receives credentials scoped to that event endpoint.
Polling anti-pattern -> events (with EEM for partner governance).
Enterprise use cases
D4
Cloud Pak for Integration

A bank's payment hub must: accept payments over APIs, guarantee no loss, process in order per account, provide real-time fraud scoring on a stream, and let other teams consume payment events. Which design is MOST appropriate?

API Connect/DataPower for intake; ACE puts each payment onto MQ (persistent, transactional) for guaranteed processing; after processing, events are published to Event Streams keyed by account ID (ordering per partition) and consumed by Event Processing for fraud detection and by other teams
Everything over Kafka with acks=0
Everything over synchronous REST, with no messaging
Aspera for payment files only

The design uses each capability for its strength: governed API intake, assured transactional processing on MQ, then an event backbone with per-key ordering via the account ID partition key, Flink-based fraud detection, and fan-out to other teams.
Correct: it combines governed intake, assured delivery, keyed ordering and stream processing.
Wrong: acks=0 risks losing data.
Wrong: synchronous REST couples availability and lacks event fan-out.
Wrong: file transfer does not meet real-time API needs.
Account-keyed events ensure all transactions for an account land in the same partition, preserving order for downstream consumers.
Kafka ordering is per partition, so 'ordered per account' means keying by account ID.
Enterprise use cases
S2
App Connect Enterprise
An integration must expose an existing MQ-based back end as a REST API for a mobile app. What is a typical CP4I implementation?
An ACE REST API flow that converts JSON to the back end's message format, uses MQ request/reply with correlation IDs, and is published and secured through API Connect
Expose MQ queues to the mobile app directly
Use Aspera to transfer JSON files
Use Event Streams compaction
ACE handles protocol and format bridging (REST/JSON to MQ messages) with correlated request/reply. API Connect adds security, rate limiting and a developer portal for the mobile channel.
Correct: ACE bridges REST to MQ, and API Connect governs exposure.
Wrong: mobile apps must not connect to MQ directly.
Wrong: file transfer is not an API.
Wrong: compaction is unrelated.
A balance-inquiry API in ACE uses MQ request/reply with a 5-second timeout and returns JSON to the app.
Protocol bridging -> ACE. Exposure governance -> API Connect.
Enterprise use cases
S3
DataPower Gateway
When might an architect deploy a standalone DataPower Gateway instance in CP4I rather than relying only on the API Connect gateway service?
When non-API-Connect gateway functions are needed, such as a multi-protocol gateway for MQ/HTTP bridging, B2B or legacy XML/SOAP security services, configured directly in DataPower
When no gateway functions are needed at all
When only Kafka topics need management
DataPower can never run outside API Connect

DataPower can run as an enterprise gateway instance (DataPowerService) for custom gateway services such as multi-protocol gateways, web service proxies and XML firewalls, independently of API Connect.
Correct: standalone DataPower serves custom gateway scenarios.
Wrong: then no gateway is needed at all.
Wrong: Kafka management is Event Endpoint Management's job.
Wrong: DataPower is available as a standalone CP4I instance type.
A logistics company uses a DataPower multi-protocol gateway to bridge partner AS2/HTTP traffic onto internal MQ queues.

Add more firewall rules
Increase server timeouts
Ban all integrations

Delete the whole namespace
Restart every node in the cluster
Reinstall OpenShift

Group flows into runtimes by business domain and change cadence (and by non-functional needs such as scaling or isolation), avoiding both one huge runtime and 300 single-flow runtimes
Put all 300 flows into a single runtime
Create one runtime per flow regardless of size
Group flows alphabetically

The sender channel to the remote queue manager is not running (for example retrying because of a network, TLS or name mismatch)
The local queue is persistent
The consumer is too fast
